items.title: AI’s hidden storage bill: What inference leaves behind
items.raw_text: Ask most executives to picture the cost of AI and they’ll likely see GPUs—racks of accelerators with gigawatts of power—and a waitlist for silicon. But that picture leaves something out: Data storage costs. What happens to data after a model responds? Much of the back-end data that’s generated—from billions of daily prompts, images, and videos—needs to be stored. But data storage is one of the harder infrastructure costs to plan for, and it’s often overlooked in initial AI infrastructure planning. As inference scales, the data footprint grows with it Traditionally, AI infrastructure conversations have centered on the compute-intensive process of training a model. Training is finite: a run starts, burns through compute, and ends. But inference runs continuously, every time a model answers a prompt. For infrastructure planning, that difference matters: A training run is a project you can budget for and retire. Inference doesn’t retire; every inference request leaves something behind. Take AI-generated video. In this workload, the back-end spend can be significant. From internal measurements, WD found that an 8-second clip (returned to a user as a 3.97MB 720p file) left more than 500MB of associated data behind on the back end, including logs, cached context, immediate renders, backups, and safety records. items.title: Strengthening Europe through public libraries: OMC report to be launched in Dublin
items.raw_text: Public libraries are part of everyday life. They help people read and learn, access culture, develop digital skills and connect with others. The OMC report brings together evidence of this work and makes the case for stronger support. On Wednesday, 28 October 2026 , the report will be officially launched at an event in Dublin. Strengthening Europe Through Public Libraries was developed by an Open Method of Coordination group (OMC) of 36 experts from 25 EU Member States , with input from neighbouring countries. The group reviewed legislation, national and regional strategies, funding arrangements and more than 100 examples of good practice from across Europe. The scale of the public library network is remarkable. Around 67,000 public libraries across Europe receive an estimated 757 million visits each year and serve 75 million registered users . This gives libraries a unique ability to connect European and national priorities with the needs of local communities. The report looks at ten areas in which public libraries already make an important contribution. These range from literacy, lifelong learning and access to culture to digital inclusion, democratic participation, health and wellbeing, environmental sustainability and community resilience. items.raw_text: As IFLA approaches its centenary, work on the future of libraries and on IFLA100 is well underway. Governing Board member Lisa Janicke Hinchliffe has agreed to serve as chair. Today, IFLA is inviting nominations and expressions of interest to help populate the Panel. Why librarianship, and why now? Much of the current futures conversation focuses on libraries: their services, spaces, collections and roles in communities. This Panel adds a complementary focus on librarianship: professional identity, values, education, practice and international connections. The two strands reinforce each other, because libraries can only be as strong as the profession that sustains them. What will the Panel do? Develop a working definition of international librarianship, giving discussions a shared starting point. Identify key considerations for IFLA (members, volunteers, staff and others) in reflecting on the present and future of the profession. Develop a white paper presenting these as a resource, not a policy document, for discussion and adaptation by members and units. items.title: Tesla profits drop 43% in Q3
items.raw_text: Tesla published its third-quarter 2026 financial results this afternoon. Earlier in October, it reported its sales and deliveries for the three-month period, selling fewer cars than in the same quarter in 2025 , yet it still beat analyst projections. Now we can see how those sales translate to the bottom line. Tesla brought in $28 billion in revenue in Q3, almost the same as in 2025. Automotive revenues were $20.6 billion, a 3 percent decrease year over year. Perhaps more troubling is the decline in revenue from solar panels and storage batteries—this line of business had been growing, but for Q3 revenue fell 16 percent year over year to $2.9 billion. Services and other revenues, though, which include parts and Supercharger use, grew by a third to $4.6 billion. But the company—like the rest of us—has seen its expenses go up. Operating expenses rose by 39 percent to $4.8 billion, dropping the company’s operating margin to just 2.6 percent; in Q3 2025, Tesla’s margin was 5.8 percent. Net profit fell to $787 million, down 43 percent year over year. What’s more, capital expenditures were up by 110 percent to $4.7 billion, and free cash flow was down 62 percent to $1.5 billion. items.raw_text: Smart TVs running operating systems from Samsung, Vizio, and Roku continue sending data to automatic content recognition (ACR) endpoints after users opt out of tracking in the devices’ settings, according to research published on Monday. The paper from Northeastern University researchers points to potential privacy violations from some of the biggest TV brands. ACR captures video screenshots or audio clips from smart TVs and sends the data to remote servers, where it's used for things like measuring content viewership and serving targeted ads. The paper, "Watching the Watchers: Privacy Analysis of US Smart TV Automatic Content Recognition," examined eight smart TV OSes across 12 smart TVs from 10 manufacturers (Amazon, Hisense, LG, Roku, Samsung, Sony, Supersonic, TCL, Vizio, and Westinghouse) to examine when smart TVs use ACR and how effective opting out of user tracking is. We didn't think remote-controlling a local agent was end-game for how people would run agents, so we built a new product where the agent runs in the cloud, any client can talk to it through an API, and it can still use your laptop as one of its machines. items.title: Review: Carrie is a triumphant remix with one major flaw
items.raw_text: Carrie White, the telekinetic prom queen from hell, is one of the most beloved horror icons in popular culture. First introduced in Stephen King's 1974 novel, Carrie , the character was immortalized in director Brian De Palma's 1976 adaptation, widely regarded as one of the best horror films of all time. It's certainly one of the best King adaptations. So Mike Flanagan faced a massive challenge when he signed on to create an eight-episode miniseries for Prime Video based on the book, released just in time to mark the 50th anniversary of de Palma's film. I was among the skeptics who questioned why a Carrie miniseries was even necessary, although as a diehard Flanagan fan ("Flana-fan"?), I was willing to give him the benefit of the doubt. If anyone has an affinity for smartly adapting horror in general, and King's work in particular, it's Flanagan. And you know what? With one (very big) exception, Flanagan pulls it off, giving us a richly textured version of the story that is as much about kindness and lost innocence as bloody, vengeful rage—although we get plenty of the latter, too. (Many spoilers below for the novel and the 1976 film , but there are no major reveals for the new series until after the second gallery. We'll give you a heads-up when we get there.) items.raw_text: Hey HN, this is Andy from Respan ( https://www.respan.ai ). We are building an open-source Rust AI gateway. It is a decoupled gateway, so everything is a plugin, including different providers, protocols (MCP, voice), modalities (images, videos), and gateway features (fallbacks, PII redaction, smart routing). Instead of packaging tons of providers and features into one gateway, Respan provides a small core and public interfaces that teams can use to assemble the AI infrastructure their application needs. That way, users can build their own features as additional plugins without having to change the gateway's core. Here’s a video demo: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pVv2ibXiTXM There are countless LLM gateways and most of them solve a common problem: calling different providers from a single endpoint. items.title: GTIA lanceert alliantie voor veilige inzet van ai door msp’s
items.raw_text: Hoewel de regels en werkwijzen ervoor nog volop in ontwikkeling zijn, wordt ai snel een nieuwe dienst die managed service providers kunnen verkopen. De internationale brancheorganisatie GTIA (voorheen bekend als CompTIA) wil het it-kanaal ondersteunen met een wereldwijd ai-kompas: standaarden, richtlijnen en best practices voor het leveren van ai-diensten aan het mkb. De GTIA (Global Technology Industry Association) heeft daarvoor de Managed Intelligence Alliance opgericht. Dit onafhankelijke programma helpt it-dienstverleners om ai op een veilige, verantwoorde en doordachte manier aan het mkb aan te bieden. Aanleiding is dat traditionele managed service providers (msp’s) steeds vaker de rol aannemen van managed intelligence provider (mip). In die hoedanigheid leveren ze ai-agenten en automatiseringsdiensten, in plaats van alleen fysieke hardware of servers. Het idee voor de alliantie kwam oorspronkelijk van cloudmarktplaats Pax8, dat als charterlid betrokken is. Vervolgens is het initiatief ondergebracht bij GTIA om een breder gedragen ecosysteem te vormen. GTIA heeft Carlo Tortora Brayda di Belvedere aangesteld om de dagelijkse werkzaamheden van de alliantie te leiden. Hij legt in een gesprek uit dat de deelnemende dienstverleners een belangrijke stem in het programma krijgen. items.title: Nieuwe vaardigheid: begrijpen wat een ai-opdracht kost
items.raw_text: Hoeveel kost al dat geprompt en gechat eigenlijk? Niet alleen in euro’s maar ook in energie? GreenPT maakt ai-gebruik inzichtelijk. ‘Kosten en energie zijn bij ai sterk met elkaar verbonden. Wie efficiënter omgaat met tokens en modellen, ziet dat meestal terug in beide,’ aldus ceo Robert Keus. Generatieve ai ontwikkelt zich in hoog tempo van experimentele technologie tot een vaste bouwsteen van bedrijfsprocessen. Verschillende afdelingen gebruiken echter verschillende modellen, leveranciers en abonnementen. Daardoor ontstaat al snel een versnipperd landschap waarin nauwelijks centraal zichtbaar is hoeveel tokens worden verbruikt, welke toepassingen de grootste kosten veroorzaken en hoeveel rekenkracht en energie daarvoor nodig zijn. Volgens Robert Keus, medeoprichter en ceo van GreenPT , is dat een risico zodra ai op grotere schaal wordt ingezet. ‘Zolang een paar medewerkers af en toe een ai-model gebruiken, lijkt het allemaal overzichtelijk. Maar zodra ai onderdeel wordt van tientallen processen en honderden medewerkers ermee werken, moet je precies weten wat er gebeurt. items.title: Kort: HPE stuurt ai naar de maan, Microsoft zet Copilot op kostenmeter (en meer)
items.raw_text: In dit nieuwsoverzicht: HPE schiet ai-rekenkracht naar de maan, Microsoft verandert Copilot in variabele kostenpost, Doccle schakelt Enable U in voor Nederlandse groei, Dutch trekt miljoenen uit voor 36 zorgsimulaties, en VPRO schetst risico’s van Europese tech-afhankelijkheid. HPE test ai-computer op de maan Hewlett Packard Enterprise ( HPE ) wil eind 2026 een computer naar de maan sturen om daar toepassingen voor ai en high-performance computing te testen. De compacte, speciaal voor de ruimte ontwikkelde computer, Spaceborne Computer-4 gedoopt, gaat mee aan boord van een rover van het Amerikaans ruimtevaartbedrijf Astrolab, tijdens een missie naar de zuidpool van de maan. Nasa en Deloitte testen eveneens toepassingen op het systeem. De computer moet grote taalmodellen, beeldherkenning en de verwerking van LiDAR-data uitvoeren. Daarmee willen de partijen onderzoeken hoe ai kan helpen bij terreinkartering, navigatie en wetenschappelijk onderzoek . Voor HPE moeten de proeven bovendien uitwijzen hoe betrouwbaar geavanceerde rekenkracht onder de extreme omstandigheden op de maan kan functioneren. Nasa test daarnaast ai-modellen voor het analyseren van gegevens en documenten, terwijl Deloitte een systeem beproeft dat cyberinbraken moet detecteren.
